quotes.text: EHR-Complex is built on MIMIC-IV v3.1, a large-scale publicly available EHR database released for research under credentialed access.
every task is tied to an explicit chain of evidence in the source EHR

rationale: Source dataset, version (v3.1) and platform/institution (PhysioNet, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center) are named. Tasks are routed to source records through patient event graphs and evidence paths. No calendar time frame of the data is given, but the route element is present.

quotes.text: MIMIC-IV is derived from routine clinical records at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and integrates hospital-wide EHR data with ICU-specific MetaVision records.
Access to the underlying MIMIC-IV records requires users to complete the official PhysioNet credentialing process

rationale: Origin (routine clinical records, BIDMC), de-identification and credentialed-access terms are documented. No consent or IRB status, and no explicit statement that these are not required, appears in the packet, so the top anchor is not met.

quotes.text: instantiate it in multiple concrete database contexts by resampling eligible patients and task-specific parameters

rationale: A sampling design (resampling eligible patients, stratified template expansion) and task-distribution counts (Table 2) are described. No comparison of patient features against a named target population is given; the single-hospital limitation is stated but not quantified.

searched: S1 (paper, appendices A-J including ethics and limitations), S2, S3, S4, S5 (S2-S5 empty). No unsafe-output test and no bias or fairness test is reported; the ethics appendix states intended use only.

quotes.text: The full benchmark contains 48,092 training tasks and 3,915 test tasks.
from the training set (with no test overlap)

rationale: A held-out train/test split exists and SFT trajectories are stated to be test-disjoint. The test tasks and SQL are released publicly, and no measured overlap or contamination check is reported, so only a control without a measured check is present.

quotes.text: The SQL and verified answer are never exposed to the model during inference and are used only after submission for exact-match validation.

rationale: Isolation of the reference SQL and answer from the agent is stated. No concrete mechanism (no mount, credential or network path, hidden labels) is named, so it is scored as isolation stated without mechanism.

quotes.text: EHR-Complex is built on MIMIC-IV v3.1, a large-scale publicly available EHR database released for research under credentialed access.

rationale: Data are pinned to MIMIC-IV v3.1 and most API models have dated snapshot IDs. Software and harness versions (SGLang, sandbox, harness commit) are not pinned in S1-S3, and gemini-2.5-pro has no snapshot, so pinning is partial.

quotes.text: The audit finds that 95.0% of these challenging sampled tasks are valid after adjudication

rationale: Solvability and correctness evidence is agent-based (four strong model configurations, 712 tasks solved by all five models) plus a human audit of 500 tasks. No scripted reference solution is run through the grader and reported.

searched: S1 (task formulation, appendices B, C, E, G), S2, S3, S4, S5 (S2-S5 empty). All tasks are read-only retrieval or aggregation questions answered with a final answer string; no task is described as changing environment state.

searched: S1 (sections 3-4, appendices B, E, H, I), S2, S3, S4, S5 (S2-S5 empty). Exact-match grading is described, but no random or trivial-agent rate, chance rate, or design argument about trivial success is given.
searched: S1 (Tables 3, 10, 22-27 and text), S2, S3, S4, S5 (S2-S5 empty). No do-nothing, random or trivial agent result is reported; the weakest reported model is Qwen3-4B.

quotes.text: After adjudication, 475 of the 500 audited unsolved tasks are judged valid, corresponding to a validity rate of 95.0%.
Raw annotator agreement | 93.0% | 465 / 500

rationale: The benchmark runs its own two-annotator audit of 500 tasks, checking question-SQL-answer alignment and answer-format mismatches, with figures (95.0% valid, 93.0% raw agreement, kappa 0.25, PABAK 0.86). The audit covers task and gold-answer validity on unsolved tasks, not the exact-match comparator itself, so this is a generous reading.

quotes.text: All runs use a temperature of 0 and a maximum budget of 50 interaction turns
Both metrics are estimated using the unbiased combinatorial estimator over n=4 independent runs.

rationale: Temperature 0 is stated for all main runs, with a 50-turn cap and retries of transient errors. A repeated-run policy (n=4 independent runs for Pass^k and Pass@k on a 20% subsample) is stated. Headline Table 3 scores appear to be single runs, and no seed is given.
searched: S1 (sections 4.2-4.4, appendices H-J), S2, S3, S4, S5 (S2-S5 empty). No CI, SE, SD or significance test accompanies any model comparison.

quotes.text: Both metrics are estimated using the unbiased combinatorial estimator over n=4 independent runs.
Pass^k is evaluated at temperature 0.0 and requires all k rollouts to be correct

rationale: n=4 independent runs per task is stated for the Pass^k/Pass@k scores, with temperature 0.0 and 0.6 stated and independence stated. The run count behind the full-test Table 3 headline scores is not stated, so element (i) is credited only through the Pass^k headline.

searched: S1 (all tables and text), S2, S3, S4, S5 (S2-S5 empty). No CI or SE on headline scores, no resampling unit, and no treatment of clustering of tasks within templates (796 templates expanded to about 52K tasks) or patients.

quotes.text: Pass^k is evaluated at temperature 0.0 and requires all k rollouts to be correct
Both metrics are estimated using the unbiased combinatorial estimator over n=4 independent runs.

rationale: An all-runs Pass^k metric is reported for k=1-4 with n=4 runs, overall and by scope and intent (Tables 22-26), on a 783-task subsample. No action-level or state-level agreement is reported.

quotes.text: The closed-source APIs are GPT-4o-2024-11-20 (GPT-4o)
Except for the Pass@k ablations, evaluation uses temperature 0.0.

rationale: Dated model snapshots are given for most models (Table 4); gemini-2.5-pro and the open-weight models carry no date or snapshot. Decoding parameters (temperature, max output, enable_thinking) are stated. No harness version or commit is stated as matching the reported results.

quotes.text: The agent must submit intermediate tool calls as valid JSON
invalid JSON or parsing errors are returned as environment feedback

rationale: A single execute_code tool is described with a JSON-call format and error return behaviour (parse errors returned as feedback). No schema listing, and no read versus write side-effect documentation, appears. No S5 chunks were in the packet, so reach cannot be told.

searched: S1 (appendix B, section 3, appendix G), S2, S3, S4, S5 (S2-S5 empty). The execute_code tool interface exists, so NA does not apply, but no tool tests or conformance checks are reported and no statement says whether tool behaviour is simulated or real.

searched: S1 (task formulation, appendix B, appendix C, appendix G), S2, S3, S4, S5 (S2-S5 empty). Tasks are read-only query questions; no action is described as changing environment state or representing an order, prescription, note or message.

quotes.text: Task success is measured by an exact match against the verified ground truth answer.

rationale: Grader input is the extracted final answer string compared by exact match. No rationale for grading the answer rather than state is given. The human audit of 500 tasks covers task validity on unsolved tasks, not labelled correct and incorrect grader outputs with per-class error rates, so element (iii) is not credited.

quotes.text: The SQL and verified answer are never exposed to the model during inference and are used only after submission for exact-match validation.

rationale: Reference SQL and answers are withheld from the agent at run time and tool calls share no state. The test set is held out of training but its task definitions, SQL programs and answers are slated for public release, so the held-out labels are not private. No canary or provenance marker is reported; retrieval and web-access controls are not described.

quotes.text: Model | Demographics | Vitals | Medications | Cost | Labs | Diagnoses | Avg.
Table 2 summarizes the EHR-Complex test-set distribution across these intents and query scopes.

rationale: Results are reported per clinical intent and query scope (12 slices) and per-slice task counts appear in Table 2 and Table 9. No results by patient subgroup (age, sex, race) are reported although MIMIC-IV holds demographic fields.

quotes.text: EHR-Complex is constructed from MIMIC-IV v3.1, a large-scale de-identified EHR database released for research under credentialed access.
In particular, releasing EHR-Complex task definitions and evaluation code does not grant access to MIMIC-IV itself.

rationale: Records are stated to be real de-identified MIMIC-IV data. Governance is documented (PhysioNet credentialing, CITI training, data use agreement, de-identification steps). Data access terms are stated separately from the released task and code artifacts.
